name: Bellwether
description: Historic-tower monitoring pitch with suspended bronze and archival signal records.

slides.title: BELL
items: WETHER
A listening record for historic towers
HERITAGE MONITORING / SEED PITCH

slides.title:
A familiar sound.
An unfamiliar change.
items: A keeper hears the bell every week. A subtle change in vibration can disappear into memory between inspections.
Bellwether keeps comparable recordings from the same installation, so a conservator can review a change with the original conditions attached.
The record supports an inspection decision. A specialist remains responsible for the condition assessment.

slides.title: The tower is the context
items: Every recording belongs to a bell, a mounting position and a ringing session.
The first visit records the installation, agrees access with the keeper and establishes a repeatable listening position.

slides.title:
Install once.
Compare over time.
items: A removable sensor records vibration at an agreed mounting point. Each session carries its date, ringing pattern and installation notes.
If a trace changes, the reviewer checks the recording conditions before requesting an on-site inspection.

slides.title: From strike to review
items: Listen
Capture a scheduled ringing session. Log sensor position and any maintenance since the last record.
Compare
Match like-for-like sessions. Flag a repeatable shift and retain the original trace for review.
Decide
A specialist reviews the evidence, speaks to the keeper and records the next action.

slides.title: Read the decay
items: Illustrative normalized vibration after a strike
Two comparable sessions
The faster decay is a review prompt. Mounting, temperature and ringing conditions must be checked before attributing it to the bell.

slides.title: A tower subscription
items: per tower / month
Includes scheduled recording, a retained session archive and one monthly specialist review. Installation is quoted after the access survey.
£144 direct cost

£75 review time
£39 equipment and support
£30 storage and site liaison
£96 contribution per tower-month before central overhead.

slides.title: Begin with the keeper
items: A regional cluster
Recruit through conservation practices already serving several nearby towers. Each practice nominates a reviewer and an access contact.
40 towers
At the proposed subscription, forty installations would generate £115,200 in annual recurring revenue.

slides.title: A record that survives a handover
items: Keeper changes
The next volunteer inherits recordings, installation photographs and an open-actions list.
Contractor changes
A new specialist can compare the original sessions and see why a previous decision was made.
Equipment moves
The installation gets a new baseline. The old series stays available with its position history.

slides.title: People who can interpret the signal
items: Mira Hale
Conservation lead
Owns reviewer training, access protocols and the decision record. Each escalation has a named specialist.
Owen Reed
Instrumentation lead
Owns mounting repeatability, trace quality and the equipment log. The pilot measures how often a session must be repeated.

slides.title: Three gates before expansion
items: ACCESS
Six towers complete agreed installations with a keeper and specialist present.
REPEATABILITY
At least 95% of scheduled sessions meet the recording-quality checklist.
RENEWAL
Four pilot towers renew at full price after six months of documented review.

slides.title: Keep the next century audible.
items: £480k seed
